result.title: Spaghetti Splatting: Differentiating Curvilinear Dirac Masses via Convolution
result.summary: In production systems, 3D geometry is represented by primitives such as points, lines, and triangles, as rendering hardware is optimized to generate images from them very efficiently. Learning such primitives from images by volume rendering is challenging, as they are Dirac masses defined at infinitesimal locations in space. EWA splatting, Poisson reconstruction, and 3D Gaussian Splatting overcome this by convolving Dirac masses with a low-frequency kernel, a recipe that generalizes along two axes: the kernel and the primitive. As points and triangles have already received significant attention, we investigate this recipe for curvilinear primitives, and introduce Spaghetti Splatting. We approximate curves by polylines whose convolution converges to that of the continuous curve, and volume render each segment so that connected segments composite without overcounting at their joints. For fast training and inference, we linearize the camera projection per segment, which also accommodates kernels beyond Gaussians, such as Beta kernels. As a point is a curve of zero length, our representation is a strict superset of 3D Gaussian Splatting. It remains competitive with the state-of-the-art on general scenes, outperforms methods specialized to line-like geometry, natively supports anti-aliasing, and produces long connected strands that are directly amenable to physics simulation.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究曲线原语的三维重建与渲染，提出 Spaghetti Splatting，用折线近似曲线并沿卷积核进行体渲染，每段线性化相机投影，可与 Gaussian 及 Beta 等核配合，从而从图像中学习线状几何。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于图形学中的图元表示与可微渲染工作，虽涉及 Dirac 质量卷积与核选择，但目标是图像重建而非 VLM 内部推理状态或证据使用，未提供可用于 LVR 表示、生成或停止决策的具体线索。
